To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution and mass function of the number of components greater than the ith progressively censored order statistic are derived for both the independent and dependent cases and that the distribution and the mass function are used in the development of a goodness-of-fit test.
the number of observations that exceed the ith PCOS can be used to test the goodness-of-fit of a copula to a given data set.

we provide the probability mass and the distribution function for the number of observations that are greater than the ith progressive Type-II censored statistic for the case of dependent component lifetimes and also provide a goodness of fit method for determining the copula model for dependent lifetimes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of the number of components that are greater than a given PCOS.
the number of observations that exceed the ith PCOS for a system with dependent components.
the distribution of the number of components in a life-testing problem that are close to but greater in magnitude than a given PCOS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented here provide a useful tool for the analysis of life-testing data.
the results of the present paper can be used in goodness-of-fit testing for the case of dependent components.
the results developed in this paper can be applied to a variety of situations in reliability, survival analysis and other fields of application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a new approach to the goodness-of-fit testing of the copula model.
we derive a distribution of the number of components with lifetimes exceeding a specified PCOS-II.
, we have developed a goodness-of-fit test for the Archimedean copulas based on the distribution of the number of lifetimes greater than the ith progressively Type II censored order statistic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of observations exceeding a particular PCOS-II can be used for model discrimination.
, for a given PC OS-II, the distribution of the number of components greater than it is dependent upon the copula used for modeling the component lifetimes.
the proposed method is a viable alternative to the existing goodness-of-fit methods for the case of dependent components.
